description: Wedderburn-orthogonality structural test: confirms that the off-diagonal Gram tr_M(ρ_λ(β) · ρ_μ(β)) is identically zero for distinct partitions λ ≠ μ in the per-partition basis, via the block-diagonal embedding of irreducible projections. Implication: the SDP shadow-price hypothesis in the per-partition basis is structurally equivalent to the LP-cost hypothesis (no genuine off-diagonal Gram to exploit). The richer Specht-tableau or Murphy/braid-word basis is the natural next probe to test the genuine SDP hypothesis. Class C (diagnostic / structural).

off_diagonal_gram_summary.reason: Wedderburn orthogonality: π_λ · π_μ = 0 for λ ≠ μ

data.conclusion: Wedderburn-orthogonality forces the off-diagonal Gram in the per-partition basis to be identically zero. The SDP-with-Gram in this basis equals the LP-cost ranking (per #639 cycle 6 probe: 1/3 match, T only). To genuinely test the SDP hypothesis for the per-partition k_λ selector, a richer basis is needed: (a) Specht-tableau (indexed by SYTs within each λ), or (b) Murphy/braid-word basis. Both break the Wedderburn diagonalization and supply off-diagonal Gram structure. This is the natural next probe per rem:per-partition-k-lambda-rule's open question.
